name: Red Bull school (vertical pressing)
scopeNote: Red Bull school as practised at Salzburg and Leipzig from Rangnick's arrival as sporting director in 2012 (exact day not found, partial date used) through Nagelsmann (Leipzig 2019-21) and Marsch (Salzburg 2019-21; New York 2015-18 not mined). Sources use 'Gegenpressing', 'pressing traps and trigger mechanisms' (Spielverlagerung) and Rangnick's own 'heavy metal' / 'Red Bull football'. Popular label 'gegenpressing' is incomplete: sources describe a pressing trap system with fast vertical attack, and it varies by coach: Rangnick/Schmidt man-oriented back line, Hasenhuttl trigger-based zonal press, Nagelsmann 5-2-3 with trap out wide and more possession, Marsch man-oriented 2v1 press. Nagelsmann himself moved away from 'unconditional team pressing' towards possession (RBLive 2018). Set-pieces not covered. Nagelsmann 70/30 quote has no original date; the Coaches Voice article date 2024-06-28 is used.
openQuestions: Proposed ids: ralf-rangnick exists in manager catalog; julian-nagelsmann and jesse-marsch not found in profile-audit/research/manager, proposed ids julian-nagelsmann and jesse-marsch.
Rangnick's own Red Bull-era tactical coverage is mostly via Spielverlagerung 2017 (Leipzig 2015/16) and quotes; no primary tier A study of Salzburg 2012-15 found.

Marking: Spielverlagerung says Rangnick's Leipzig back line marked strikers and Breaking the Lines says Marsch's Salzburg is man-oriented, but a search summary (unverified) called Salzburg ball-oriented; The Master Minds pages were 403.
Marsch's New York Red Bulls (2015-18) and Hasenhuttl/Schmidt as exemplars not researched; Nagelsmann's quotes undated in Coaches' Voice.
Spielverlagerung article says Hasenhuttl's Leipzig is 'in contrary to the public opinion' not full-force in first pressing phase, which contradicts the popular total-press image.

sources.title: Beyond the business model: RB Leipzig's football philosophy (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Granted, Gegenpressing was not invented in the late 2000s or early 2010s, though the conscious use of pressing traps and trigger mechanisms to force transition attacks was certainly an aspect that had rarely appeared in that specific form.

sources.title: Beyond the business model: RB Leipzig's football philosophy (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Under his supervision, Schmidt built up Salzburg as said Gegenpressing powerhouse.

sources.title: Beyond the business model: RB Leipzig's football philosophy (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Leipzig first and foremost relied on a 4-4-2/4-2-2-2 formation with two outside-in wingers and, most of the time, one auxiliary striker as a connecting piece between midfield and the players upfront.

sources.title: Beyond the business model: RB Leipzig's football philosophy (Spielverlagerung)

sources.title: Beyond the business model: RB Leipzig's football philosophy (Spielverlagerung)

sources.title: Beyond the business model: RB Leipzig's football philosophy (Spielverlagerung)

sources.title: Beyond the business model: RB Leipzig's football philosophy (Spielverlagerung)

sources.title: Beyond the business model: RB Leipzig's football philosophy (Spielverlagerung)

sources.title: Beyond the business model: RB Leipzig's football philosophy (Spielverlagerung)

sources.title: Beyond the business model: RB Leipzig's football philosophy (Spielverlagerung)

sources.evidence: Nagelsmann's Leipzig side were successful in pressing with a lone striker supported by two attacking central midfielders, with the three of them aiming to force play into traps out wide.

sources.title: Julian Nagelsmann tactics and style of play - Coaches' Voice

sources.title: Julian Nagelsmann tactics and style of play - Coaches' Voice

sources.title: A Masterclass in Pressing: Red Bull Salzburg (Breaking the Lines)
sources.evidence: Salzburg's main idea off the ball is to form situations where they are pressing with two men against one opponent with the close options for the opponent with the ball man-marked.

sources.title: A Masterclass in Pressing: Red Bull Salzburg (Breaking the Lines)
sources.evidence: Red Bull Salzburg they use a man-marking orientation to prevent opponents from being able to escape the press through passing. An advantage of this is that it is easy to coach and can be effective against a rigid structure.

sources.title: A Masterclass in Pressing: Red Bull Salzburg (Breaking the Lines)

sources.title: A Masterclass in Pressing: Red Bull Salzburg (Breaking the Lines)

sources.title: A Masterclass in Pressing: Red Bull Salzburg (Breaking the Lines)
